examples.trans: Near Anikeev's house two suspicious people were walking.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: after 'в' / 'на' the place form is 'углу' (stressed on the end): 'в углу' = in the corner

examples.trans: The café is on the corner.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.en: to be located, to be situated

examples.trans: Where is the operating room located?

Where is the operating room located here?

meanings.note: in a list or a story
in a list or a story

examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'on foot' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Let us have you walk the rest on foot.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

ехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride

meanings.en: to go, to drive, to ride
meanings.note: by car, bus, train, in one direction, now

examples.trans: Vitalik, we're going to the Santa Fe.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: professional associate (common gender, declined like feminine)

examples.text: Мой коллега помог мне с отчётом.
examples.trans: My colleague helped me with the report.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.
We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rumor, hearing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Vanya is very upset because of the rumors.

examples.text: Слухи про дедушку — это провокация Осипенко.
examples.trans: The rumors about his grandfather are Osipenko's provocation.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to summon', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Ты же не помнишь ничего. Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You don't remember anything, after all. You called a sober driver!

meanings.note: сказать лишнего = to say too much
сказать лишнего = to say too much

examples.trans: Yesterday I said too much to you.
Do you have a spare ticket?
The main thing is do not say unnecessary foolishness.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да это не воровство, послушай! Это абсолютно безопасно.
examples.trans: That's not stealing, listen! It's completely safe.

meanings.note: short form: ты прав = you're right
short form: ты прав = you're right

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to joke', paired with 'пошутить'.

examples.text: Шутишь? Правда, скажи, где деньги? Меня наняли.
examples.trans: Are you joking? Seriously, tell me, where's the money? They hired me.

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!

спешить.gloss: to hurry, be in a rush

meanings.en: to hurry, rush, be in a hurry
meanings.note: куда ты спешишь? = where are you rushing to?

examples.trans: What happened? Where are you rushing to?

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!

meanings.note: at an office, hotel, or cemetery

examples.text: Входишь сразу налево, к администратору. Там сидит такой Лисицын.
examples.trans: You go in and turn straight left, to the administrator. A fellow named Lisitsyn sits there.
